title: Christina Applegate reveals she was misdiagnosed with MS – 'Back at square one'

 Brendan Morrow USA TODAY Updated Oct. 20, 2026, 9:06 a.m. ET Hear this story Christina Applegate has shared a stunning health revelation: She doesn't have multiple sclerosis after all.
 The "Dead to Me" star, 54, revealed the news in the latest episode of her "MeSsY" podcast , a show she hosts with Jamie-Lynn Sigler that is focused on living with MS.
 Applegate had previously shared in 2021 that she was diagnosed with multiple sclerosis, an autoimmune disease. But on her new podcast episode, she said this was a misdiagnosis. Applegate broke down in tears as she recounted how her doctor recently told her, "Congratulations, you don't have MS."
 "This may come as great news, but to me, it comes as I'm back at square one," Applegate emotionally said.
 Applegate said her reaction to the news was that she was "not happy at all," noting, "You don't get misdiagnosed and then all of a sudden I'm better. I haven't gotten better, Jamie. If anything, I've gotten worse in some ways. So I'm back at square one, that I don't know what's going on with me."
 Love crosswords? Explore the Crossword page and play the new MidGrid Crossword. The star said her doctors will have to continue investigating what has been happening with her because she had "every symptom of someone with MS."
 "I had a reason … as to why my day sucked every day," she said. "And now, I don't have a reason, and it's very unnerving and it's really confusing for me."
 Applegate also got vulnerable on the podcast about feeling like she has "let everybody down" in that she and Sigler had become "poster children for MS." Sigler, though, assured her that she did nothing wrong and "didn't mislead anyone."
 The update comes after Applegate spent several months in the hospital earlier this year. She had stepped away from her "MeSsY" podcast, but returned on Oct. 20 with a two-part episode sharing her health news.
 Multiple sclerosis is a disease where the "immune system attacks the protective sheath that covers nerve fibers, known as myelin," which "interrupts communication between the brain and the rest of the body," according to the Mayo Clinic . Symptoms can include numbness or tingling, difficulty walking and fatigue.
 Applegate originally announced her MS diagnosis in August 2021, telling followers on X that it has "been a strange journey," but she has felt "so supported by people that I know who also have this condition." She has said her first symptom was numbness in her toes.
 Since then, Applegate has candidly documented her health journey on her "MeSsy" podcast and elsewhere. In a 2025 podcast episode, she said she has "been in the hospital upwards of 30 times" since being diagnosed.
